primary_decoupling.activity_to_decouple: Discover and evaluate specific packaged-water brands (compare “commodity water” options vs. provocative/viral brands with sustainability narratives)
primary_decoupling.from_incumbent_bundle: Traditional bottled-water incumbents (and the retail shelf/paid advertising system) that bundle discovery/evaluation into mass marketing + in-store placement alongside purchase
primary_decoupling.customer_pain: Packaged water is effectively commoditized, so customers must spend extra time/attention to figure out what’s actually different (brand/persona fit, sustainability claims) before they can confidently choose—turning discovery into a high-effort, low-reward step.
primary_decoupling.new_offering: Launch an AI-powered, social-native “Liquid Death Finder” that turns discovery into a 30-second quiz + short-form creator content stream, then outputs (1) the best-fit Liquid Death product/variant and (2) a “where to buy” path (nearby retailers + direct links) without requiring customers to change their normal shopping routine—i.e., “peeling away a portion of the customer’s value chain” (books/unlocking-the-customer-value-chain-chapter-1.md :: Page 10).
primary_decoupling.why_customer_switches: They get to a confident choice faster with less mental effort in a category that otherwise feels interchangeable, while still buying wherever they already shop; the experience also reinforces the provocative brand identity and sustainability narrative that motivated the search in the first place (E3, E4, E6, E8).

do_not_decouple.activity: Purchase/obtain the chosen packaged-water product from a seller (online or offline)
do_not_decouple.reason: Don’t make the wedge about rebuilding distribution/fulfillment or forcing a channel switch in a low-involvement category; that would shift Liquid Death from a brand-led decoupling into operationally heavy execution, risking the core growth engine (provocative branding + viral marketing) that is already working (E4) and competing head-on where incumbents are structurally advantaged (E3).

do_not_decouple.activity: Dispose/recycle the packaging and decide whether to repurchase, switch, or recommend
do_not_decouple.reason: Avoid taking responsibility for end-to-end recycling/logistics infrastructure as the primary wedge; it’s capability-intensive and slow-moving relative to the brand/discovery advantage, and could distract from the sustainability-led positioning without delivering a near-term, decouplable digital win (E4, E8).

do_not_decouple.activity: Notice a need for convenient, portable hydration
do_not_decouple.reason: Don’t try to “create the need moment” as a standalone product (e.g., hardware reminders, medical hydration monitoring) because the core job-to-be-done already exists broadly and Liquid Death’s advantage is differentiating choice within packaged water, not owning the entire hydration-trigger stack (E9, E3, E4).

do_not_decouple.activity: Set selection criteria (e.g., health orientation, environmental concern, and brand/persona fit) and decide to use packaged water versus other hydration options
do_not_decouple.reason: Don’t expand into generalized “health/hydration coaching” or other beverage-substitution decisioning as a wedge; it dilutes the sharp, brand-driven differentiation in packaged water and increases scope/CAC by competing across broader wellness criteria instead of winning the most decouplable weak link (brand discovery/evaluation) (E4, E6, E3).
